chunkSummary: Lines 21766-22918 hold one item, the 2026-era `class KnackError` (v1.3.0): a per-instance error reporter that enriches an error with Knack context (scene, view, event, record), user, browser and performance data, rate-limits and groups repeats, and writes a row to a configured error-log view through `new KnackAPI({debug:false, showSpinner:false}).createRecord(sceneId, viewId, data)` (L21803, L22819); it also offers six overlapping function wrappers (wrapFunction, tryCatch, monitorPerformance, monitorApiCall, safeExecute, executeFunction) plus Knack-event wrappers that must stay on jQuery because Knack fires `knack-*` events with `$.trigger` (L22283, L22323). The public surface (constructor options, 15 public methods, `options`/`api`/`boundHandleError`/`performanceData` properties) is kept verbatim with no shim; the wave-3 port collapses the six wrapper bodies and three copies of the argument serialiser onto one private core, removes dead branches (`record` is never populated so grouped duplicates always return null at L21864; L22721 duplicates L22715; the `caAPI` clause at L22548 is subsumed by `API`; both `eventSelector` branches at L22279-22281 produce the same string), fixes three latent bugs (`_getActiveViewId` returns input ids like `view_12-field_3` at L22382; Opera is never detected at L22834; `safeExecute` returns a Promise despite its `@returns {*}` JSDoc at L22160) and adds a `handle()` alias so a KnackError instance can be installed as the global `errorHandler` without breaking the four `errorHandler.handle(` call sites elsewhere in the file (L9059, L9063, L9069, L20216).

functions.proposedSignature: Identical public surface: same class name, constructor options (same names and defaults), the same 15 public methods with the same parameter lists and defaults, the same public properties (`options`, `api`, `boundHandleError`, `performanceData`) and the same underscore methods kept as-is (they are reachable by consumers, so not converted to `#private`). 'Unknown' } : { name: 'Unknown', version: 'Unknown' };` - removes the 30-line switch. Ordering bug: 'Opera' (L22834) sits after 'Chrome' and 'Safari' but Opera's UA contains both, so Opera is reported as Chrome; order the table Edge, Opera, Chrome, Firefox, Safari, IE. Detection-output change flagged in behaviourRisks.

L22884-22895 _getDeviceType: keep the regexes; note in JSDoc that iPadOS 13+ Safari sends a 'Macintosh' desktop UA so iPads report 'Desktop'/'macOS' (an optional `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1 && /Macintosh/` hint would fix it, not required).

L22900-22916 _getOperatingSystem: `return SYSTEMS.find((s) => s.pattern.test(userAgent))?.name ?? 'Unknown OS';` with the table as a frozen static (order matters: Android before Linux, iOS before macOS already correct).

Whole class: add `handle(error, additionalInfo = {}, errorSource = 'Unknown') { return this.handleError(error, additionalInfo, errorSource); }` so `errorHandler = new KnackError(...)` satisfies both call styles used in this file (`.handle(` x4, `.handleError(` x9); bump `@version` to 1.4.0; move `_validateOptions()` (L21824) before `_setupContextTracking()` (L21820) so misconfiguration is reported before listeners are bound; keep all underscore methods public-by-convention (consumers may call `_getCurrentSceneId()` / `_getBrowserInfo()` directly - every property reachable from a global class is public API per the policy).
behaviourRisks: jQuery is load-bearing here, not incidental: `$(document).on(`${eventType}.${viewId}`)` (L22283) and `$(document).on(`knack-${eventType}.any`)` (L22323) receive events that Knack raises through jQuery `.trigger`; a 'modernised' `document.addEventListener('knack-view-render.view_12', ...)` would never fire and context tracking plus wrapKnackListener would silently stop working. Keep `$` for these two sites (or route them through a single foundation helper that wraps `$(document).on`).

All wrappers (L21894, L21975, L22010, L22051, L22189) turn synchronous functions into async ones: the wrapped function's return becomes a Promise, side effects still run synchronously up to the first await, and `return false` from a wrapped jQuery event handler no longer calls preventDefault/stopPropagation. This is existing behaviour that callers may depend on in either direction; preserve it exactly, do not 'fix' by returning sync results for sync fns.

wrapKnackListener's inner handler (L22254-22277) is synchronous and only catches synchronous throws; an async handler's rejection bypasses it and surfaces as `unhandledrejection` (then via setupGlobalErrorHandling if enabled). Making it `async` would also change the handler's return value to a Promise - keep as is and document.

safeExecute (L22160) resolves a Promise (via executeFunction immediate:true, L22234) even though its JSDoc says it returns the value; existing callers may `await` it. Making it synchronous would be a signature change requiring a shim - leave it asynchronous.

Fire-and-forget `self.handleError(...)` calls inside catch blocks (L21986, L22030, L22097, L22220, L22272) are not awaited; any synchronous throw inside handleError's capture phase (e.g. `errorData.errorSource.includes` on a non-string source at L22547, or JSON.stringify on a circular `additionalInfo` at L22814 is already inside try) becomes an unhandled rejection, which setupGlobalErrorHandling(true) feeds back into handleError (bounded only by maxErrorsPerMinute). V2 should wrap the capture phase in try/catch with a console fallback - a behaviour change in the error path only.

Stored field text will change where the port fixes defects: `contextViewId` (and thus the grouping hash, L22527) changes from 'view_12-field_3' to 'view_12' when an input is focused; `browserName` 'Chrome' -> 'Opera' for Opera users; `knackContextFormatted` time text changes from browser-locale `toLocaleString()` to fixed en-GB; `functionArgs` from monitorPerformance uses 'function() { ... }' instead of '[Function]'; `pageLoadTime`/`domReadyTime` shift by a few ms when moving off the deprecated `performance.timing`. None affect code paths, but any Knack report/filter built on the literal strings will see the new values.

Grouping and rate-limit state (`_errorHashes`, `_errorCount`) is per instance and `_errorHashes` is never evicted (L22468-22474); over a long-lived SPA session it grows by one entry per distinct (name|message|source|scene|view|event) tuple. Adding eviction (e.g. drop entries older than an hour on each insert) is a safe memory fix but changes when a repeat is treated as fresh if done carelessly - keep the one-hour reset semantics at L22452-22462.

setupGlobalErrorHandling (L21928) is not idempotent: each call adds another `error`/`unhandledrejection` listener, so calling it from two scripts double-logs. Adding a guard is a small behaviour change (second call becomes a no-op) - acceptable but must be called out in the changelog.

The constructor eagerly instantiates KnackAPI (L21803) with `{debug:false, showSpinner:false}`; the KnackAPI port must keep those option names and defaults, and `instance.api` must stay a plain writable property (consumers may inject a stub API in tests, and `instance.api.getRecords(...)` is reachable public API).

Dropping the `Object.assign(additionalInfo, ...)` mutation at L21855 means a caller's object is no longer enriched with `contextSceneId`/`contextViewId`/... after `await handleError(err, obj)`. No caller in this file reads back from the object it passed; the stored record is unchanged. Negligible but technically a side-effect change.

_validateOptions (L22420-22431) only console.errors; it never throws, so a misconfigured instance silently degrades to console-only logging. Keep that (throwing from the constructor would be a thrown-errors signature change).
`Knack.router.current_scene_key` (L22342) and `Knack.getUserRoleNames()` (L22642) are relied on from memory - unverified against live docs. Keep the DOM fallbacks that exist today.
functions.knackPractice: Mostly follows the documented model: it tracks context from the documented jQuery lifecycle events (`knack-view-render.any`, `knack-scene-render.any`, `knack-form-submit.any`, `knack-record-update.any`, `knack-cell-update.any`, `knack-record-delete.any` at L22320-22323, with the (event, view, record) payload shapes), reads `Knack.getUserAttributes()` / `Knack.getUserRoleNames()` / `Knack.application_id` for user and app identity, and writes through the view-based KnackAPI (`createRecord(sceneId, viewId, data)` at L22819, so no object-based key ever reaches the browser). It fights the model in three small ways: it infers scene/view from the DOM (`.kn-scene` at L22347, `[id^="view_"]` at L22382/L22397) even though it already receives `view.key` from the events it listens to; `_extractSceneIdFromUrl` (L22409) expects `scene_123` in the URL whereas Knack's hash router uses scene slugs, so that fallback never matches in production; and the `view_` prefix test does not distinguish Knack's `#view_x` roots from `#view_x-field_y` inputs. `Knack.router.current_scene_key` as the authoritative scene key is unverified against live docs. Error rows are created with the public key `knack` + user token through KnackAPI, which is the sanctioned browser-side write path (unverified against live docs for rate-limit specifics; KnackAPI handles 429 backoff).
functions.rationale: KnackError is a 2026-era class (v1.3.0, JSDoc throughout, async/await, optional chaining) that the policy places in wave 3: port as-is with dead-code removal and consistency fixes, no signature changes. The rewrite earns roughly 450 lines by collapsing six wrapper variants and three argument serialisers onto one private core, deleting dead branches (never-populated `record`, duplicated context list, duplicated recordId assignment, dead `caAPI` clause, identical `eventSelector` branches) and table-driving the user-agent sniffing, while every public and underscore method keeps its name, parameters and return type. Risk is medium rather than low because this is the error path itself (failures here are invisible), because its two jQuery bindings must survive the jQuery-removal drive, and because several defect fixes (`_getActiveViewId`, Opera detection, en-GB timestamp) alter the text stored in the Knack error table and therefore the grouping hash. The additive `handle()` alias is the one new surface, and it closes a real trap: four call sites in this file use `errorHandler.handle(` while the class only offers `handleError`.

crossCuttingFindings: Method-name split on the global error handler: the console fallback at L15-33 defines both `handle` and `handleError`, this file calls `errorHandler.handle(` at L9059, L9063, L9069 and L20216 and `errorHandler.handleError(` at nine sites (L12556-L13019, L21311, L21731), but KnackError (the class an app would install as `errorHandler`) only implements `handleError`. With `errorHandler = new KnackError(...)` the four `.handle(` calls throw `TypeError: errorHandler.handle is not a function` inside an error path. Fix both ends in V2: add the `handle` alias to KnackError and standardise the library's own call sites on one name (recommend `handleError`, the majority and the class's native name; the policy text currently names `handle`).

App-specific identifier in the library: `'caAPI'` at L22548 is a consuming-app source prefix; it is also dead because any string containing 'caAPI' already matches the preceding `includes('API')`. Remove it; grep for other app names (GAP-Track/Spot wrappers) in error-source strings across chunks.

Knack lifecycle events can only be observed through jQuery (`$(document).on('knack-...')`): this file has nine `$(document).on(` sites (two in this chunk at L22283 and L22323). The V2 'no jQuery' target must carve out an explicit exception for Knack event binding, ideally through a single foundation helper (`onKnackEvent`, proposed above) rather than nine independent `$` touches.

Scene and view discovery is implemented four ways: KnackError._getCurrentSceneId (L22340) / _getActiveViewId (L22374) / _getFirstViewId (L22396), getBackgroundSceneId (L18641), knackNavigator.getCurrentSceneInfo (C02, L630-657) and the getViewRootElement / bulkActionFindViewRoot / getViewMountElement family. KnackError's variants contain the `view_x-field_y` false-positive and a modal-unsafe `.kn-scene` query; they should delegate to the canonical primitives chosen in wave 1.

additionalInfo objects passed to errorHandler across the file carry DOM elements, jQuery objects and Knack view/Backbone models (e.g. `{ viewElement }` at L9063, `{ target }` at L20216, coordinator state at L12556-12559). KnackError stringifies that blob with plain `JSON.stringify` at L22814; a circular structure throws, is caught at L21877 and only console.error'd, so the error record is silently lost exactly when the context is richest. A shared cycle-safe `safeStringify` (proposed above) should be a wave-1 foundation primitive used by KnackError and any other serialising helper.

Only one other place sniffs the platform (`navigator.platform` at L7175 for Cmd/Ctrl labelling); no dedupe needed with KnackError's UA tables, but V2 should keep all UA inspection inside KnackError rather than spreading it.

KnackError constructs `new KnackAPI({ debug: false, showSpinner: false })` (L21803) and calls `api.createRecord(sceneId, viewId, data)` (L22819): the KnackAPI port (its own chunk) must keep those two option names, their defaults, and the three-positional-argument createRecord contract. Declaration order in V2 does not matter for this (construction happens after script evaluation), but KnackAPI should still precede KnackError for readability.
Three JSDoc blocks in this chunk are indented 8 spaces (L22044, L22433, L22769); a repo-wide lint rule for JSDoc indentation would catch the same drift in other recent classes.
